transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

I came in because... well, since my grandson was killed, things just haven't been right. My daughter, she'll come over and sit right beside me, holding my hand. And I know I love her, I do. But... I just cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore. It's like that feeling is just gone.
How long ago did your grandson die?
It was six days ago. He was killed right outside the community center. So, this has been going on for those six days.
Since your grandson died, have unwanted memories of what happened come into your mind when you do not want them to?

Yes, they do. It happens when I'm just trying to do normal things. I'll be folding a quilt square, or... or reaching for my tea, and all of a sudden I hear those shots again. I see him lying there outside the community center. It's like it is happening right in front of me, and I just can't stop it from coming into my head.
Since your grandson’s death, have you felt detached from yourself or as though the world around you is unreal?

Yes, actually. It's a very strange feeling. Sometimes my own living room just looks... flat and strange. It's almost like I'm looking at it through church glass or something. And... well, sometimes I feel as if I'm just watching this old woman move around the house, instead of actually being fully in my own body. It's like I'm not really there.
Since your grandson’s death, have you been deliberately avoiding people, places, conversations, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yes, I have. I absolutely will not go near that street. And... well, people keep calling about the repast at the center, but I just don't answer the phone. I can't deal with it right now. I also find myself turning off any second-line music the instant it comes on. I just shut it off immediately, because hearing it... it just pulls me straight back there to what happened.
Since your grandson’s death, have you felt constantly on guard or watchful, as if danger could happen again at any moment?
No, I wouldn't say I feel like that. I just... I mostly just stay in the house, you know? I haven't really felt like I need to be on the lookout for danger or anything like that.
Since your grandson died, have you had trouble sleeping?
No, my sleep has been about the same. I just go to bed like usual. I haven't really noticed any trouble with it.
Since your grandson died, have you been more easily startled by sudden noises or movements?

Yes, I have. It's actually been quite noticeable. Um, if the ice maker drops cubes in the kitchen, or if a car backfires down the block, my whole body just jumps. I jump so hard I have to grab the table to steady myself. And my heart... it just keeps pounding and pounding for a long time, long after everyone else has already settled down.
